amendments.body: In `e2e_habitat_geometry_probes.rs`, the `all_habitat_geometry_probes_summary` test (#[test]) calls the same `run_probe_*` functions that the 5 individual `#[test]` probe functions also call. When `cargo test` runs the full file, each expensive probe (multi-day simulations) executes twice: once in its own test and once in the summary. Either gate the individual tests behind a feature flag / `#[ignore]` when the summary runner exists, or have the summary runner reuse test results rather than re-executing. This doubles CI wall-clock time for no additional coverage.
amendments.rationale: The e2e habitat probes are computationally expensive (hundreds of simulated hours each). Running them twice per test invocation wastes CI time and can cause timeouts in constrained environments.

amendments.body: In the biofilter scaling probe (`run_probe_biofilter_scaling_bigger_media_faster_cycling`), the `(None, None)` match arm for `reduced_n_clearance` was changed from `record_failure_all` to a silent no-op (`{}`). This means if both the small AND large filter fail to clear reduced nitrogen to the threshold within the entire 504-hour duration, no check is recorded and the probe silently passes. Add at minimum a `record_check` with a warning or a non-fatal note so that total clearance failure is visible in the probe summary report, even if not treated as a hard failure.
amendments.rationale: Silently ignoring the case where neither filter clears nitrogen is a test coverage gap. A complete failure of both arms to process nitrogen could indicate a broken nitrogen cycle subsystem, and should at least be flagged in the summary report.

amendments.body: In `root_oxygenation_active_biomass_g` (substrate.rs:136-161), the function calls `compute_habitat_registry(state)` to build a fresh registry every time it is invoked. Since this function is called from `substrate_oxygenation_breakdown` which is called from `step_substrate_zones` on every hourly tick, AND `compute_habitat_registry` iterates through all habitats and plant guilds, consider accepting the registry as a parameter or caching it. The engine step sequence refreshes habitats at multiple points; passing the already-computed registry would avoid redundant work on every tick.
amendments.rationale: Performance concern. `compute_habitat_registry` is non-trivial (iterates geometry, hardware, plants, substrate) and is already called and stored on `state.habitat_registry` at multiple points in the engine step. Recomputing it inside the inner-loop substrate step adds unnecessary overhead, especially as tank complexity grows.

amendments.body: In `step_substrate_zones` (substrate.rs:71-73), the same `effective_penetration_cm` is written to every substrate layer regardless of layer position or properties. This means in a multi-layer stack (e.g., 2cm sand over 3cm porous substrate), the bottom layer gets the same `o2_penetration_depth_cm` as the top. While the zone geometry methods correctly interpret this as a global boundary from the top of the stack, the field name `o2_penetration_depth_cm` on each individual layer is misleading — it reads as 'penetration within this layer' rather than 'global boundary from substrate surface'. Add a doc comment to `SubstrateLayerState::o2_penetration_depth_cm` clarifying that this is a global stack-relative boundary, not a per-layer local depth.
amendments.rationale: Maintainability risk. Future contributors may misinterpret `layer.o2_penetration_depth_cm` as local to the layer and write incorrect zone geometry calculations. The field semantics are non-obvious and the existing tests rely on the global interpretation.

payload.summary: The root-zone oxygenation implementation is well-designed and correct. The core ROL formula in `substrate_oxygenation_breakdown` (exponential saturation capped by substrate depth) is scientifically sound and properly parameterized via `rol_rate_cm_per_g`. Guild filtering correctly excludes `FastStem` plants. All 8 unit tests and 5 integration tests pass. Tracing output properly exposes base penetration, ROL bonus, active root biomass, and effective penetration as separate metrics. The diff under review (e2e probe test updates) correctly adapts the habitat geometry probes to work with the new ROL feature: the substrate redox probe now uses live rooted plants instead of manually seeding substrate state, and the biofilter probe switches to reduced-N (TAN+NO₂) tracking. No correctness bugs were found in the implementation itself. The four amendments address: (1) doubled test execution from the summary runner, (2) a silently-ignored failure case in the biofilter probe, (3) redundant habitat registry recomputation on every tick, and (4) a misleading field name for multi-layer stacks.
